A1.justification: Both PDFs describe EraseDiff by the same authors. Their text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison despite substantial revisions.

before.justification: V1 reports original diffusion-unlearning experiments on CIFAR10, UTKFace, CelebA and CelebA-HQ, including quantitative results, generated examples and appendix analyses.

after.justification: V3 reports original DDPM and Stable Diffusion experiments, including comparative performance, computational measurements, ablations and additional appendix results.

M1.justification: The documented update changes: v3 Section 3.2 subtracts the forgetting-loss gradient at the inner endpoint, whereas v1 Algorithm 2 treats the terminal inner loss as constant. Adaptive weighting, already optional in v1, becomes the standard algorithmic rule. V3 also introduces alternative-concept prediction targets and restricts SD nudity updates to non-cross-attention layers, while retaining the basic retain/forget objective.

E1.justification: CIFAR10 class unlearning remains, including the DDPM airplane case already present in v1 Figure 20. V3 removes UTKFace and CelebA/CelebA-HQ race/attribute experiments and random-sample forgetting. It adds text-to-image class erasure on Imagenette, nudity evaluation using I2P and generated nudity prompts, and retained-utility evaluation using COCO30K prompts.

E2.justification: V3 adds evaluated SA and SalUn comparisons on DDPM, ESD/SA/SalUn for SD nudity, and ESD/SalUn for tench erasure. Retraining and two-stage TS comparisons disappear. V1's simultaneous-optimization comparator SO corresponds to v3's MOO comparator; this is not an entirely new comparison method.

E3.justification: The main evaluation shifts from DDIM per-class FID, accuracy, MIA, output KL divergence and weight distance to DDPM retained-class FID over 45K images, precision/recall and classifier entropy/probability. New SD protocols specify 50 sampling steps, prompt-based sampling, NudeNet thresholds and COCO FID/CLIP evaluation. V3 also defines peak-memory measurement across preparation and forgetting, while timing only the forgetting stage.

E4.justification: V1's extensive retained-data-size, epoch, noise-distribution, guidance, FGSM and two-stage analyses are removed. V3 reports revised DDPM step-size/inner-iteration ablations and new SD target-prompt, detector-threshold and flagged-image checks. Simultaneous optimization and generated-retaining-data analyses persist under the DDPM setting in v3 Table 5 rather than being wholly new analyses.

E5.justification: V3 Table 4 newly states that runtime is averaged over five runs; v1 reports approximate runtimes without specifying repetitions. This establishes new repetition and aggregation reporting, not an increase in runs for all experiments. Neither version supplies confidence intervals or seed-based dispersion for the main quality results.

E6.justification: V1 Figure 20 reports airplane/DDPM FID 8.90 at 200 steps; v3 Table 1 reports 7.61 with an explicit 45K retained-image protocol. Identical evaluation conditions are not established, so this is a revised report rather than a verified same-setting gain. New SD results include FID 17.01/CLIP 30.58 after nudity erasure and FID 1.29/forgotten-class probability 0.00 after tench erasure. The earlier face/DDIM result tables disappear.

T1.justification: V3 introduces a constrained update-direction problem and a KKT derivation in Theorem 3.1, while removing v1's detailed KL-based loss and DDIM derivations. The Pareto-optimality result already exists in v1 Appendix B and is rewritten and moved to Theorem 3.2. V3's printed multiplier in Theorem 3.1 is inconsistent with Equation 9.

C1.justification: The central retain-utility/erase-information goal persists, but v3 makes gradient-conflict handling and Stable Diffusion concept erasure central contributions, replacing the earlier emphasis on class/race/attribute removal across face and object datasets. The introduction adds specific claims of approximately 11-fold and twofold DDPM forgetting-stage speed advantages over SA and SalUn, respectively.

C2.justification: V3 adds interpretations linking improved FID but reduced recall to possible overfitting, and higher classifier entropy to stronger erasure. It acknowledges residual tench-like characteristics and poorer data-free performance relative to SA in Table 5. These concrete qualifications replace v1's emphasis on acceptable utility degradation and its discussion of unstable MIA evaluation.

D1.justification: V3 adds an EraseDiff code-access link, specific DDPM batch-size/learning-rate/200-step settings, and SD checkpoint, learning-rate, trainable-layer and synthetic-training-data instructions. These disclosures do not establish that the earlier airplane experiment used different settings. V1's detailed model sizes, baseline training recipes and DDIM/face-model schedules are removed; reported hardware changes from A40/A100 to A5500/A100.

R1.justification: V3 substantially repositions EraseDiff against diffusion-specific unlearning, expanding comparisons with SA and adding SalUn, Forget-Me-Not and learnable-prompt-erasure references. It emphasizes competing methods' computational requirements and forgetting/utility tradeoffs. V1's MAML distinction and plug-and-play loss positioning are removed.

P1.justification: The abstract and optimization narrative are extensively rewritten. Experiments change from effectiveness/utility/comparison subsections to model-specific DDPM and SD sections. The Pareto argument moves from the final appendix into the method section, and the appendices are reorganized into Details and Additional Results.

P2.justification: V3 introduces a first-page SD montage, extensive SD comparison grids, nudity-count charts and compact metric-by-method tables. These replace much of v1's class-by-class tabulation, MIA/KL histograms and face imagery. Ablation displays, title/author formatting, typography and page composition are also substantially redesigned.

improvement.justification: V3 addresses v1's limited direct comparison with diffusion-specific unlearning methods through SA/SalUn/ESD evaluations and SD tests, while adding concrete failure qualifications. This makes the comparative claims more informative. The net gain is limited by the removal of retraining, MIA/FGSM evidence and detailed baseline recipes, together with the inconsistent multiplier in the new optimization theorem.
